reviews.one_line_contribution: An item-level placement law for distilled agent experience: a label-free statistic — the fraction of *deployment* queries for which an item would enter top-k ("coverage breadth") — decides whether that item belongs in the always-on instruction or the retrieval bank, and the payoff of promotion is claimed to be the top-k slot it vacates rather than the promoted text itself.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, one conceded and one not. (a) Conceded: working-set estimation and frequency-based cache admission. The proposal's own Related Work admits that "estimate future access from a deployment-representative window rather than stale logs" is working-set estimation, and that MemGPT/A-MEM instantiate the usage-frequency version in LLM agents; running MemGPT-style promotion as arm E2(v) caps the damage but also caps the contribution. (b) Not conceded, and more damaging: the paper's claimed *inversion* — "promotion is valuable because it vacates a slot in the competitive tier, a benefit with no analogue in caching" — is false as stated. Exclusive cache hierarchies (victim caches, exclusive L2/L3) are defined by the property that promotion into the fast tier removes the block from the slow tier and frees its capacity, and that is exactly why they are used. Separately, admission policies built around cache pollution and scan resistance (LRU-K, LIRS, ARC, TinyLFU/W-TinyLFU) exist precisely because high-frequency or high-recency items crowd out items that would have served other requests, and their standard remedy is to *refuse admission* to polluting items — i.e. the crowding-out mechanism this paper presents as new is the textbook motivation for admission control. Once the inversion argument fails, the remaining differences the proposal lists (accuracy rather than hit rate, content/framing change on promotion, always-full tier) are real but are differences of setting, not of claim, and the surviving novelty is "we measured a known allocation principle in an LLM-agent memory bank." That is a workshop-sized delta unless the empirical results are unusually clean. Third, in dense-retrieval terms breadth is hubness: because each calibration query admits exactly k items, Σ_m b(m) = k identically, so "broad" items are just the embedding-space hubs of the query distribution, and hubness correction (Radovanović et al.) and MMR-style diversification are prior art on the same phenomenon.
reviews.strongest_objection: The mechanism claim contradicts the measured result the track brief tells the proposer to treat as the starting position, and the proposal misreads that result as support. The pilot found that *injection volume* was the causal lever: cutting seven retrieved items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank, with topically correct retrievals. Slot competition predicts the opposite sign of the same intervention. E3 stakes the entire mechanism on P3, "hybrid-with-refill beats hybrid-without-refill by ≥3 EM points at k=2" — that is, adding back a lower-ranked, more marginal item helps. The pilot says adding items hurts. No-refill at k=2 is literally the volume reduction (k=2→1) that the pilot's 7→3 result says should be the *better* arm. If the pilot generalizes, P3 comes out backwards and the paper's own refutation clause fires ("the benefit is token savings, not slot competition"). Worse, the matched-token constraint in E2 means the hybrid cannot win by volume reduction either: the consolidated block is present on every episode and the freed slots are refilled, so total injected experience per episode is held roughly constant by construction, while the pilot says total injected experience is the only lever that moved anything. Under a straightforward reading of the prior results, the modal outcome of E2 is that breadth hybrid ≈ pure top-k ≈ MemGPT promotion at matched tokens, all within the 2.5-point indistinguishability band, and P2/P3/P4 all resolve to "placement does not matter once tokens are matched." Second-order but also serious: E1, the "core test," has an effective sample size of 14 for the tested quantity. Four item-level fixed effects (b, u, f, length) on 14 items leaves ~9 residual df; the 150 queries per item and the query random intercept inflate nothing for an item-level slope. And the 75/75 stratification of the 150 queries into m∈top-k and m∉top-k equalizes exposure across items by construction, which is the very thing breadth is supposed to vary — A(m) measured on an exposure-equalized set is not the placement advantage that obtains in deployment, and the stratification mechanically attenuates the breadth coefficient the paper needs to be positive.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Three changes, in priority order. (1) Reconcile with the pilot before running anything: add the volume-monotonicity curve (accuracy vs. k at k=1,2,3,4 with a fixed bank) as E0(c) and state, pre-registered, what P3's refill-beats-no-refill prediction implies given that curve's slope. If accuracy is decreasing in k in this setup, the refill prediction is already refuted and the design must change; if it is flat or increasing, the pilot's volume result does not transfer and the proposal should say so up front rather than citing volume harm as confirmation of slot competition. (2) Turn the dialed-in skew into a law. P4's effect size is a free parameter: the authors choose the Zipfian skew of the history stream, so "breadth beats frequency by ≥3 points" measures the knob, not the world. Sweep the skew (report effect size against KL(history‖deployment) at three or four levels, reusing the same bank) so the claim becomes a dose-response relation rather than a single manufactured contrast; this also subsumes the unskewed positive control at no extra design cost. (3) Fix E1's estimand and power: drop the 75/75 stratification in favour of sampling queries i.i.d. from the deployment distribution (so exposure varies with breadth as it does in deployment), and raise the item count from 14 to ~40 at n=60 each — the same 4,800-episode envelope buys 2,400 more effective df on the only coefficient the paper calls its core test. Separately, either uncap the MIPROv2 arm or drop it: a 400-rollout MIPROv2 on a 7B is a strawman and losing to it would be uninformative, while beating it proves nothing.
reviews.missing_baseline: A de-hubbed / diversified fixed-k retriever at the same k and the same token budget — the retrieval-side fix for exactly the phenomenon the paper attributes to placement. Concretely: (a) MMR or DPP-diversified top-k, and (b) a hubness-corrected score (CSLS, or per-item mean-similarity subtraction / query-side centering) computed from the same 500 unlabeled calibration queries breadth already uses, so it costs zero extra labels and zero extra episodes. This is the baseline a reviewer will demand because the identity Σ_m b(m) = k makes "high breadth" and "embedding hub" the same property: if simply preventing hubs from monopolizing top-k recovers the hybrid's gain, then nothing was learned about instruction-vs-bank placement, the entire consolidation apparatus is unnecessary, and the finding reduces to "dense retrieval over a small memory bank has a hubness problem." Drop-only (E3c) does not cover this — it deletes broad items outright, whereas de-hubbing keeps them retrievable for the queries they genuinely fit, which is the strictly better policy the paper never tests. A distant second omission: MemGPT-style promotion computed on the *calibration* stream rather than the skewed history, which would isolate "fresh data" from "coverage statistic" and reveal whether P4's win is anything more than the conceded working-set-estimation principle.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin — it is empty, and the proposal says so: the search tool failed on every invocation, zero titles were retrieved, and the closest-work list is explicitly recollection. The honesty is creditable and the pre-committed withdrawal clause is more than most submissions offer, but under this track's own standard an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness, not a neutral, and this is the second or third round in which it has gone unfixed. Judged on content: the decision problem is already occupied by MemGPT's core/archival paging and A-MEM's consolidation, which the proposal concedes and now runs as arm E2(v); the statistic is occupied at the level of principle by working-set estimation, also conceded; and the "inversion" that is supposed to survive both concessions is contradicted by exclusive cache hierarchies and by pollution-aware admission control (TinyLFU/LIRS/ARC), which the check does not consider. That leaves the collision surface larger than the proposal's own assessment admits. On live preprints, the most likely scoop is in the agentic-context-engineering / playbook lineage the proposal already cites: ACE-style "grow-and-refine" curation with de-duplication and merging of repeatedly-useful bullets into a persistent context is one step from "consolidate the items that keep getting retrieved into the always-on block," and context-budget-allocation and hot/cold memory-tiering preprints in the Mem0/Letta/ReasoningBank orbit are exactly the natural next paper. I cannot name a specific title with confidence and will not invent one — but that is precisely the burden the submitters have to discharge and have not, so I score novelty as unestablished rather than absent. The stated commitment to a dated search log is the right remedy and should be executed before, not after, the experiments are run, since a collision would redirect which of E1/E3/E6/E8 becomes the paper.

reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim that where a distilled agent-memory item should live (merged into the always-on instruction vs left in a retrieval-gated bank) is decided by a label-free coverage statistic — the fraction of unlabeled deployment queries for which the item enters top-k — and that the payoff of promotion is the top-k slot it vacates for narrow items, not the promoted text itself.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two bodies the proposal never names. (1) Hubness in high-dimensional nearest-neighbour retrieval: b(m) is exactly the k-occurrence statistic N_k(m) of Radovanovic et al. (JMLR 2010), and the known pathology is that a few hub vectors enter the top-k of almost every query and crowd out relevant neighbours. The established remedies — hub demotion, local/global score centering, mutual-proximity, CSLS — remove the crowding without any instruction tier, so the proposal's central mechanism has a documented cause and a documented cheaper fix. Adjacent to it, Maximal Marginal Relevance (Carbonell & Goldstein 1998) and result diversification already solve 'a fixed-size result set is wasted on redundant, always-ranked items.' (2) ACE-style agentic context engineering and Mem0-style consolidation already perform grow-and-refine with semantic de-duplication of a growing always-on block, which is operationally 'consolidate the broad, keep the narrow retrievable' without the theory. MemGPT and working-set estimation are correctly conceded. Note also that the Related Work's load-bearing novelty argument — 'fast-tier residency does not free slow-tier capacity' — is false for exclusive cache hierarchies (Wong & Wilkes, DEMOTE, USENIX 2002), where promotion is precisely eviction from the lower tier; the 'inverted optimal move' is therefore a weaker discriminator against caching theory than the proposal claims.
reviews.strongest_objection: The matched-token protocol is arithmetically incompatible with the mechanism the paper wants to demonstrate, and the incompatibility loads the headline test. Arm E2 (vi) is base prompt + consolidated block C + k retrieved items with freed slots refilled; arm E2 (ii) is base prompt + k retrieved items. The hybrid is strictly longer by |C|, so 'mean realized prompt tokens within 5%' can only be achieved by inflating pure top-k — either raising its k, or appending the neutral filler of ablation (e). Both inflations are already known from this track's own pilot to be harmful: cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank, i.e. injection volume is the established causal lever. So a >=3 EM win for the hybrid over pure top-k (P2) is predicted by the volume effect alone, with zero placement content, and the paper would be re-deriving its own starting position under a new name. E3's padding control does not rescue this, because it pads the hybrid's freed slots rather than testing a token-matched no-consolidation arm. Compounding this, P2 anchors the hybrid only against pure top-k and pure playbook: given a pilot in which the full bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven, the hybrid can satisfy every one of P2, P3, P4 and P5 while still losing to the no-memory arm that E2 (i) runs but no prediction references — a placement law that is beaten by having no memory at all is vacuous, and nothing in the pre-registration forecloses that outcome.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes. (1) State the token-matching operator explicitly and pre-register it: match by holding the retrieval slot count k identical across arms and equalizing tokens with a token-matched drop-only-plus-filler arm, and report the accuracy-versus-tokens curve as primary rather than any single matched point; if matching is done by raising k for the baseline, the contrast must be pre-declared as confounded with volume. (2) Add a pre-registered superiority test of the breadth hybrid against the no-memory arm at matched tokens, and state up front that failure to clear no-memory voids P2-P5 regardless of their internal outcomes. (3) Run E1 condition (c), item absent entirely, on all 14 items rather than 4, and regress the contrast acc(instr) - acc(absent) on b(m) alongside acc(instr) - acc(bank); as designed, the breadth coefficient in P1 is close to a tautology, since removing a broad item from the bank necessarily perturbs top-k on nearly every query while removing a narrow one perturbs almost none, so the current slope measures slot-vacating and cannot separate consolidation from deletion. (4) Fund the utility estimator to a precision at which it could win: 6 paired probes per item on 60 of 300 items leaves u(m) with a standard error on the order of the effects being routed on, and leaves 240 items with no utility value at all, so 'coverage beats utility' and 'utility is not a significant predictor after conditioning on breadth' are both largely guaranteed by estimator noise. Pre-register the diagnostic that if utility routing lands within noise of the random-routing arm in E4, the utility comparison is declared uninformative rather than won.
reviews.missing_baseline: Breadth-penalized (hub-demoted / MMR-diversified) fixed-k retrieval: leave every item in the bank and subtract a calibrated function of b(m) from the retrieval score, or apply standard hubness correction / MMR diversification, so narrow items surface into top-k without any instruction tier, any consolidation LLM call, or any extra tokens. This is the arm a retrieval-literate reviewer will demand, because it delivers the paper's own claimed mechanism — vacate the slot the broad item was occupying — at strictly lower token cost, and if it matches the hybrid the entire instruction-vs-bank placement framing collapses into a re-ranking heuristic. Drop-only (E3 c) is not a substitute: it deletes the item from the system entirely rather than demoting it, and it is not token-matched to the hybrid. Secondarily missing: a token-matched drop-only arm (broad items removed, no consolidated block, tokens padded to the hybrid's budget), which is the only clean isolation of what the consolidated text contributes.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin — it is empty, and the proposal says so: the web search tool failed on every invocation, zero titles or dates were retrieved, and the closest-work list is explicitly recollection. By the standard that an unsearched claim of novelty is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is the single largest deduction, and it is aggravated by the proposal's own note that two prior review rounds flagged it and it remains unfixed; the commitment to run a dated search log before submission is a promise, not evidence. The proposed query list is also blind in the direction where the real collision lives: it searches the agent-memory and context-engineering vocabulary but never the retrieval vocabulary (hubness, k-occurrence, hub reduction, result diversification, MMR, redundancy-aware re-ranking), which is where the coverage statistic and its standard remedy already exist. I cannot name a specific mid-2025-to-present preprint that runs the refill/no-refill/padding controls, so the mechanism controls plausibly remain unclaimed; but the decision problem is MemGPT's, the statistic is working-set estimation applied to a hubness quantity, and dedup-under-capacity of an always-on playbook is already implemented in ACE-lineage and Mem0-style consolidation systems, so the residual novelty surface is much narrower than the proposal asserts and remains unverified.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A label-free routing rule for distilled agent experience: an item belongs in the always-on instruction rather than the retrieval bank in proportion to its coverage breadth (the fraction of unlabeled deployment queries for which it enters top-k), and the payoff of promotion is the top-k slot it vacates rather than the text it adds - the latter isolated by refill / no-refill / padding controls at k=2.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, one conceded and one not. Conceded: MemGPT/A-MEM-style capacity paging plus OS-flavoured hot/warm/cold agent-memory tiering (the 2025 MemoryOS-type line), which already promotes by access heat into an always-resident tier, and working-set estimation, which already says estimate future access from a representative recent window rather than stale logs. The proposal's stated differentiators (tiers are not latency-equivalent, the competitive tier is always exactly full, the payoff is the vacated slot) are real and the refill/no-refill/padding controls are a genuinely unrun experiment, so this is a narrowing rather than a kill. Not conceded, and more damaging: the in-context-example selection literature, which has scored candidate exemplars by coverage over an *unlabeled* target pool for years - vote-k selective annotation (Su et al., ICLR 2023) picks a representative subset by graph coverage of unlabeled deployment queries with zero labels, and DPP/CEIL-style diversity selection exists precisely because redundant broad exemplars crowd out complementary ones. b(m) is also, mechanically, a retrieval hubness score: hubs that appear in many top-k lists, and demoting them (mutual proximity, local scaling, CSLS, MMR) is a known and cheaper intervention that needs no instruction tier at all. That b(m) is simultaneously a hubness statistic and a coverage statistic is never acknowledged, and it means the proposal has an untested rival explanation and an untested cheaper fix.
reviews.strongest_objection: The two headline contrasts are decided by measurement budget and by an absent comparator, not by the theory. (1) P4 asks breadth routing to beat utility routing by >=3 EM, but u(m) is estimated from 6 probes on each of 60 items. A per-item paired estimate at n=6 has a standard error on the order of 15-20 EM points; utility routing is therefore a random permutation of the top-60 items with a faint signal, and b(m) is computed on 500 queries with no sampling noise at all. Breadth will beat utility at that budget even if utility is the true causal variable, so P4's central comparison cannot distinguish the hypothesis from estimator noise. Worse, arm E2 (iv) pure playbook is built by merging the *highest-utility* items, so the same 6-probe noise handicaps the playbook baseline that P2 must beat by >=3 points - the two thresholds that would be reported as the paper's result are both partly artifacts of how little was spent estimating the rival statistic. (2) P2 never requires the breadth hybrid to beat E2 (i) no-memory. The track's own starting position is that this bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven, and that write-path repairs neutralized harm without converting it to gain; E0's gate explicitly passes when the bank matters in the harmful direction. So the fully satisfying outcome - hybrid beats top-k by 3, beats playbook by 3, beats MemGPT-style promotion by 3 - is compatible with every memory arm sitting below the no-memory arm, i.e. with the recommended system being worse than deleting the memory subsystem. A hybrid that wins only by injecting less of a harmful bank is a volume result, which the pilot already established, not a placement law. Secondary but sharp: E1's 75/75 stratification equalizes bank-side availability across items by construction, which removes the main channel through which breadth is supposed to act and makes the regressed A(m) not the deployment placement advantage; and the tested quantity is an item-level fixed effect estimated from 14 items with four item-level predictors, from which P4 additionally asserts a null (utility and frequency not significant after conditioning on breadth). An absence-of-effect claim from 14 items is uninterpretable, and the likeliest confound - breadth correlates with item abstractness, so general strategy text belongs in an instruction for reasons that have nothing to do with slot economics - is controlled only for item length.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Five changes, all inside the stated envelope. (1) Equalize the routing-statistic budget: either give utility a fair estimate (30+ probes on fewer items, or a shrinkage/hierarchical estimate with reported reliability) or, better, degrade breadth to the same information budget by recomputing b(m) from a 6-query subsample and showing breadth still wins - and report the split-half reliability of b, u and f, since no comparison of routing variables is interpretable without it. Route the pure-playbook arm by something other than the noisy u as well, or report it under both selection rules. (2) Pre-register hybrid vs no-memory at the same >=3-point bar, put no-memory on every accuracy-versus-token curve, and state explicitly that no headline is claimed if no-memory is the best arm. (3) Add the missing E1 cell (d): item in the instruction AND retained in the bank. Cells (a) instruction-only, (b) bank-only, (c) absent and (d) both give a clean item-level decomposition of availability versus slot-vacating, and (d) is the cheapest possible direct test of the inverted-caching claim - far cheaper than resting the mechanism entirely on the admittedly underpowered k=2 refill/no-refill contrast. Replace the 75/75 stratification with deployment-proportional sampling plus inverse-probability weights so A(m) estimates the quantity the theory is about. (4) Add MMR / hubness-corrected retrieval (below). (5) Expand E1 to at least 30 items or delete every null claim about u and f. Finally, the search log promised in the Commitment section has to be run before, not after, the design is frozen, because a collision would change which arms matter.
reviews.missing_baseline: Diversity- or hubness-corrected top-k retrieval at identical k and identical tokens - MMR re-ranking, or a hub-demotion score such as mutual proximity / local scaling / CSLS applied to the same bge-large index. This is the baseline that most directly threatens the paper: it removes broad items from the competitive tier on a per-query basis, frees exactly the slots the hybrid claims credit for, requires no instruction tier, no consolidation, no LLM merge and no calibration labels, and it is what a retrieval person would reach for on being told that a few items enter almost every top-k list. If MMR captures most of the hybrid's margin, the contribution collapses to a retrieval-normalization result. Also omitted: the E1 (d) cell (item in instruction and left in bank), which isolates slot-vacating from availability at item level; a bank-deduplication / near-duplicate-merge control, since broad items are plausibly near-duplicates and drop-only does not separate deduplication from breadth; and a per-query oracle-k arm. Separately, the MIPROv2 arm (E2 vii) is capped at 400 rollouts, which is well under what MIPROv2 normally needs to converge on a multi-hop ReAct program, so as specified it is a weakened baseline rather than an honest test of instruction+demonstration coupling; the cap needs justification or a convergence curve.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is the weakest possible collision check: zero searches were run, every web-search invocation failed, and the closest-work list is explicitly recollection. The proposal deserves credit for saying so plainly rather than dressing up a stale list, and for converting MemGPT-style usage promotion from foil into a first-class arm - but candour does not substitute for a search, and by the standard that novelty must be established rather than asserted, this proposal has not established it. The tool failure is also not a complete excuse: the omissions I consider most damaging (vote-k / selective-annotation coverage selection over unlabeled pools, DPP-diversity exemplar selection, and the retrieval hubness literature) are indexed, years-old work that a recollection-based list should have surfaced, so the gap is substantive and not merely unverified. On live preprint risk, the proposal names the right danger zone and I share its assessment: the mid-2025-onward context-engineering / agent-memory-tiering line (ACE-style playbooks, ReasoningBank-style banks, OS-style tiered memory with heat-based promotion, context-budget allocation papers) is exactly where a hot/cold promotion or instruction-versus-retrieval budget allocation paper would land, and I cannot rule out that such a preprint already exists; what I would expect it *not* to contain is the refill/no-refill/padding triad and the threshold-retrieval difference-of-differences, which is the correct fallback the proposal identifies. Recommendation: the dated search log promised in the Commitment section should be a precondition for this proposal advancing, not a pre-submission chore, and it should be extended to cover exemplar-coverage selection and hubness, which the current framing does not know it needs to search for.
